- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- backfilling-provenance: Filling a pack's empty provenance files from its history - each entry derived from the adding commit, its pull request and the version log before the rule is re-read, every commit that touched the pack weighed whether or not a draft covers it, and the README and manifest trimmed to use in the same change. Use when a pack under packs/ or .claudinite/local/packs/ carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill or write a pack's provenance.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- changing-pack-elements: What a change to a pack's element owes - the entry on its provenance file, which kind, and how to append it - and what a pack's README carries. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md, skills, checks, tasks, manifest, README or provenance folder, in a repo's local pack or on a canon's shelf.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.

input.title: Recommend a code-phase timeout per task from its own run history
input.body:
Blocked-by: #2262
Model: opus

<!-- filed by /do-later -->

Every task declares `code_work_timeout`, and nothing has ever checked those numbers against what the code phase actually costs. They were picked when each task was written and have not been revisited since, so they are almost certainly far too generous — a timeout well above the real distribution buys nothing and lets a wedged run hold its lane for the whole ceiling.

The owner's instruction, verbatim in substance: prod every task toward a much lower TTL for its code phase, based on real task execution data — compare actual run time against the declared timeout, and recommend roughly **50% above the 90th percentile run**.

## The data already exists

`.claudinite/local/tasks-usage.GENERATED.json`, written by `claudinite-tasks/tasks-usage-fold`, carries per-run phase wall times including `code-work`, keyed by run id, at hour, day and week tiers. It carries **samples, never quantiles**, deliberately — a week's p90 is not derivable from its days' — so whatever reads it takes the quantile itself over whatever window it draws.

Note the fold appends and never recomputes, and a phase that did not happen leaves no key rather than a zero. A task with too few samples to support a p90 has no recommendation, and saying so is the correct output — do not invent one from three runs.

## Where this should live

No task reviews usage and recommends anything today. All 32 declarations were read while filing this:

- `claudinite-tasks/tasks-usage-fold` records the data but runs no agent and opens nothing but its own regenerated file.
- `basics/ci-performance` runs an agent over run history, but its subject is CI workflow duration regressions and it ships to every member.

So this is most likely a small task of its own in `claudinite-tasks`, agentless, weekly, reading the fold and delivering a pull request that edits the `code_work_timeout` of each task whose declared value is materially above the recommendation. Decide the distribution model before writing the first file.

## Done looks like

- A recommendation per task with enough samples, derived from that task's own `code-work` phase times, not a repo-wide figure.
- A task with too few samples named as such rather than given a guess.
- The declared timeouts that are materially off moved, in one pull request, with the numbers behind each change in its body.

## Ruled out by the owner

Nothing about the heartbeat, the executing leash, the agent leash, or cancelling an executor's Actions run. That whole direction was considered and declined on 2026-09-22 — the TTL route is what replaced it. A lowered `code_work_timeout` must stay below `EXECUTING_LEASH_MS`, which the task contract already validates.

Filed: [#2266](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2266), marked for the queue and blocked behind [#2262](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2262), model `opus`. It comes back to you for review rather than merging itself.

## A–B–C: done, and on the PR

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **A** cadence prose | done | `de45a2d` — the comments claiming an hourly scheduler and ~2h recovery |
| **B** the merge | done | `6dd696b` — repair phase, effect threading, the whole-open listing, the torn-adoption fix, the dead `supersede` op, the phase timer |
| **C** delete the task | done | same commit — `tasks/task-janitor/` gone, slot sweep with it, tests moved with their titles |
| **rule C** | done | `ac1fd93` — restored, bound read from idleness, regression pinned by a test that bites when I put the old clock back |
| **D** cancel at reclaim | dropped | your call; nothing touches the heartbeat, the leashes or the Actions run. Replaced by #2266 |

Three commits on the branch, 3803 tests passing, the one failure identical on `main`, and the world sweep's findings byte-for-byte what they were before the branch.

## What is left

**Yours:** review and merge [#2262](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2262). That is the only thing blocking the rest.

**Mine, the moment it lands:**

- **E** — dispatch the scheduler workflow and read its run log: one pass, the repair lines present, no janitor item filed, and the drain gate's count including anything the phase freed. This is also where the converge proves it: this repo's own standing janitor item, if it holds one, closes itself obsolete when the executor picks it and finds no task at HEAD.
- **G** — file the retrospective, with its brief written from what this change assumed: that recovery landing in the same pass measurably shortens the time an item spends unpickable, and that the repair phase's own wall time stays negligible against the tick. Both are now readable off the fold, since the phase is timed.

**F is moot** — it was "verify a reclaim cancels its run", and nothing cancels a run any more.

One judgment call I made without asking, worth naming: you said keep the legacy sweep alive as a placeholder. I kept the *home* rather than the code — a documented section in the repair phase saying what belongs there, what the slot sweep was, and why its rules went — plus the pure helpers and their tests in `dispatch.mjs`, uncalled but intact, so a future legacy rule has both a place to go and a shape to copy. It costs no reads on a quiet tick, which is the other thing you asked for.

> ⚠️ Still open: your review of [#2262](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2262) — E and G run here as soon as it merges.

content.text:
Comment class: other
Both answers, the second one honestly.

**Did everything pass, simulator included?** Yes. The last full run: **3804 pass, 1 fail** — `engine-pack-lane-shims`, which fails identically on `main` (a missing `engine/pack_loader/token-estimate.mjs`) and is nothing to do with this branch; I checked by stashing and running it against `main`. The simulator is inside that number: **83 scenarios, 0 failures**, plus its coverage gate. `check_the_world` reports findings byte-identical to what it reported before the branch existed.

**Did I add janitor scenarios to the simulator?** No — and your asking made me look properly, which found a real gap.

What I had done was rewire: the simulator used to fire `janitorBody` on a daily clock tick of its own, calling `sweepQueue` directly, so no test had ever exercised the janitor's instantiation, precondition, pickup or converge. That body is gone and its verdicts are recorded off the scheduler run's ops, so the existing scenarios — S11's agent leash, S18's stale-ready and stuck dependency — now run through the merged pass instead of a parallel machine. That is coverage *moved*, not coverage *added*.

The gap was that nothing in the world model asserted the thing the merge exists for. The unit tests pinned it — the threading, the same-pass lane release — but a unit test cannot show a tick doing it end to end. So `S81` now does: an item no executor can reach, the stale-ready rule taking it out of the queue, and the assertion that **no `scheduler-run` entry separates that escalation from the occurrence the same tick files**. Mutating the threading so a repair's effect is invisible to the ask turns it red on precisely that line. It closes its own loop too — the occurrence that tick files runs clean, which is what supersedes the park the same tick raised.

Two things fixed on the way: the simulator's `janitor-close` record is `repair-close`, and the quarantine lever's comment no longer names the janitor as the thing that would notice an unreachable item.

Pushed as `3baff8b` on [#2262](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2262) — four commits now.

**The TTL follow-up is withdrawn.** [#2266](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2266) is closed and its `task:origin:ad-hoc` mark removed, which matters: left marked, the next scheduler run would have adopted it into real work.

> ⚠️ Still open: your review of [#2262](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2262) — the forced scheduler run and the retrospective are mine to do the moment it merges.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
6. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

The merge leaves the local checkout on the branch it squashed, and no step here syncs `main`; the
merge is usually a session's last act. Only if you go on to start further work in this session,
sync first, before branching off anything:

```
git fetch origin main && git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main && git remote prune origin
```

# Fetching from the web

- **Needing exact text** — a summarizing fetch tool is not a source; when the bytes matter, `curl`
  into the scratchpad and read from disk. (needing-exact-text)
- **A `403`** — don't retry and don't try a sibling URL; attribute the search snippet to the
  publisher instead of asserting it, and mark it for re-verification. (a-rule)
- **A sandbox or proxy denial is a policy boundary, not an obstacle to route around** — no
  open-network runner, no ad-hoc CI workflow, no push-triggered probe to make the request from
  somewhere the policy does not apply. Answer from committed reference material or ask the owner,
  and say plainly that anything unverifiable is unverified. (sandbox-proxy-denial)
- **An explicit egress block** (`EGRESS_BLOCKED`) is domain-wide, unlike a publisher's `403`:
  working down alternate sources for the same fact spends the same denial on each. Never file the
  gap as "re-verify next pass" — no later agent pass can cross a policy block either; mark it as
  needing a human or an unblocked environment. (explicit-egress-block)

1	# claudinite-tasks — scheduled work
2	
3	Everything whose subject is task work: the work-item queue, the executor, the task contract and
4	its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, and the delivery lane a task's output
5	lands through. Declaring this pack is what gives a repo scheduled work; a repo that does not
6	declare it runs none, which is a supported state rather than a degraded one.
7	
8	The mechanism itself — the state machine, the generator, the executor's protocol, urgency and
9	forcing, recovery — is the canon's own tasks-dispatch design document, and authoring a task is the
10	`writing-tasks` skill's subject. This file is the pack's own map.
11	
12	## Layout
13	
14	Every module sits in the ROLE it plays, and the graph between the roles is
15	one-directional. `contract/` and `items/` are what everything agrees on and name no
16	stage; `world/` holds the only modules that reach outside the run; the stages sit on
17	top of those and never import each other sideways or upwards. The `tasks-stage-barriers`
18	and `tasks-world-edges-live-in-world` checks are what hold the shape.
19	
20	| Path | The role |
21	|---|---|
22	| `src/contract/` | what a task DECLARES and what its declaration means: the declaration's shape and defaults, the term vocabulary and the precondition seam every caller asks through, cadence and anchor arithmetic, the auto-merge policy engine, task discovery, dormancy |
23	| `src/items/` | the work item as DATA, over the vocabulary and grammar `public/` defines: the queue listings, the run record, the pick order over the open queue, the heartbeat |
24	| `src/world/` | the only outward edges, each a named port — `github.mjs` (every REST path this pack calls, as a named operation), `actions.mjs` (the runner's environment) with `hold.mjs` and the three env bags beside it, `sessions.mjs` (the routine fire that starts an agent), `git.mjs`, `processes.mjs`, `clock.mjs` |
25	| `src/signals/` | the collectors a precondition is handed, read through the ports and described in the contract's terms |
26	| `src/schedule/` | the tick: the repair phase that runs first, then which declared tasks have a window open and the items filed for them |
27	| `src/execute/` | the executor: claiming a ready item, running its code-work, handing it to an agent session |
28	| `src/session/` | what runs INSIDE a work-item session: converging the item, verifying its outcome, the exec record, dispatch resolution, and the automerge verdict as a command |
29	| `src/deliver/` | turning a run's output into a landed pull request or a regenerated file |
30	| `src/recover/` | repair: the queue's repair rules, workflow-failure escalation, the dead-run continuation |
31	| `src/adopt/` | what an adopting repo receives: the workflows converged from the stubs, the per-repo cron minute |
32	| `queue/` | `tasks/implement-request/` — the engine's own built-in task. Its `task.md` is a redirect kept for work items minted before the move (retired 2026-10-15); the spec itself is `public/implement-request.md` |
33	| `stubs/` | the two workflow files an adopting repo receives |
34	| `public/` | **everything outside this pack may reference** — the vocabulary and grammar `src/` builds on, the import surface, and the documents a routine reads. See below |
35	| `tasks/` | this pack's own tasks: `usage-fold` (it folds this mechanism's run records and outcome labels), `tasks-usage-fold` (what the machinery itself cost - runs, billed minutes, API calls, outcomes, parks, latencies) and `verify-production` (coded production validations - URL probes judged as code-work) |
36	| `worldRules/` | the task-declaration checks |
37	| `workRules/` | the armed-auto-merge gate (`automerge-policy-scope`) |
38	| `declared-checks.json` | `tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` — the guard over this pack's published surface, which runs wherever the pack is declared |
39	| `test/` | the unit suite, mirroring `src/`, and `test/sim/` — the simulator and its scenario suite, the mechanism's executable spec |
40	| `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` | the mechanism as claims, each citing the test that proves it |
41	| `src/deliver/deliver-pr.md` | the landing procedure every PR-delivering task's worker is pointed at, beside the lane it describes |
42	
43	## `public/` — everything outside this pack may reference
44	
45	One folder, one promise: **a name in `public/` does not move.** Everything a routine reads, another
46	pack imports or a member's own local pack names lives here, and nothing else of this pack is
47	addressable from outside. A member's `.github/workflows/` runs the entry points under `src/`
48	named by the two stubs, which are this pack's own files and not an outside caller.
49	
50	Another pack's code may import `packs/claudinite-tasks/public/*` and nothing else of this pack;
51	the `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory, and no other pack gains an
52	equivalent surface by existing. **A member's own `.claudinite/local/packs/**` reads it the same
53	way**, through its mount (`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/public/*`): the nightly
54	converge replaces `.claudinite/shared/` and may never touch a member's own packs, so an import
55	aimed anywhere else is one this repository cannot repair when the layout behind it moves.
56	
57	### Documents named from outside
58	
59	| Path | What names it |
60	|---|---|
61	| `instructions.md` | a repo's work-item routine, as a stored prompt in its console settings |
62	| `implement-request.md` | the machine block of every issue adopted into the queue |
63	
64	### Modules other packs import
65	
66	Three of the five are the DEFINITION, and `src/` imports them from here: the vocabulary, the
67	grammar over it and the GitHub client import nothing of `src/`. The other two are the
68	machinery's own operations under a stable name.
69	
70	| Module | What it publishes |
71	|---|---|
72	| `task-constants.mjs` | every value the queue writes and reads: the work item's labels, markers and body fields, the leases, the commit trailers, the declaration defaults, the pack's own parameters, the two workflow file names |
73	| `work-item-grammar.mjs` | the parse and serialize over that vocabulary — the title grammar that is an item's identity, the status and outcome decode over its labels (every legacy spelling included), the body fields, the machine block, the commit trailer |
74	| `github.mjs` | the GitHub client (`makeGh` and the run's call count), `dispatchWorkflow`, and the tracker issue a recurring task logs every run to |
75	| `delivery.mjs` | `deliverGenerated` — a regenerated file landed on a pull request that lands itself — and the landing lane's five names for a worker that lands its own pull request |
76	| `task-declaration.mjs` | the declaration's executable contract: the loader, its validation, the precondition evaluator the executor runs at pick, and the auto-merge policy engine |
77	
78	A module publishes **named** exports rather than `export *`: the list in the file is the promise,
79	so a reader sees the whole surface in one place and an internal rename can neither widen nor
80	narrow it. A consumer needing something absent asks for the named export to be added here —

11	
12	Every occurrence of every task is an issue in this repo — a `[claudinite-work]` item whose labels
13	are its state — so write the task against that queue, never a runner of its own.
14	
15	**A cadence is one of a task's conditions, not what a task is.** A task is a unit
16	of the repo's own work with preconditions, a code-work phase and optionally an
17	agentic-work phase; its `preconditions` say when the queue runs it — a cadence term
18	(`schedule:at-most-daily`) beside whatever else must hold, or no
19	`preconditions` at all, for work that runs only from an item somebody created. Work
20	that fires on an event, on a condition, or on a force is a task in exactly the same
21	sense as work that fires nightly, and reads the same contract. Anything reachable
22	from the executor belongs here rather than in a workflow of its own; see the cron
23	rule below for the narrow case that genuinely cannot be.
24	
25	Three responsibilities, strictly separated (owner, 2026-08-06):
26	
27	1. **The scheduler run** — a vendored Action
28	   (`.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`, two ticks a day) over the issue
29	   list: **ask** every task on the schedule, through its own preconditions,
30	   whether it wants to run now, and file its item only on a yes — a no is a log
31	   line, and the next tick asks again; **ready** blocked items whose wait has
32	   passed; **reclaim** dead executor claims. It keeps no calendar and no state:
33	   a task's cadence is one of its conditions, read off its own run history in
34	   the queue.
35	2. **The executor** — a pull worker over the queue (the scheduler run's post-scheduler run drain,
36	   and a `labeled`-event run for latency) that picks the next ready item, claims
37	   it, evaluates **that one task's** precondition, runs its code-work, and either
38	   converges the item or hands off to an agent session.
39	3. **The repair phase** - the first thing the scheduler run does, before it asks
40	   any task: everything about the queue that is *nobody's task* - items stuck
41	   ready past their period, items wearing no state label after a torn transition,
42	   parks their own world has since answered, and a health review of the open set.
43	   It runs first because what it frees is what the ask and the drain gate read.
44	
45	The engine is vendored under `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/`; the basics
46	pack owns the conformance guards for the surfaces a repo authors around it —
47	scheduling is baseline Claudinite discipline, present wherever basics is
48	declared (everywhere), not an opt-in feature.
49	
50	There is no watermark, no per-run state and no calendar: an occurrence exists
51	because its issue exists, and a task's history is its issues, which is why an

59	  **:10-:50** and a repo-hashed hour (written once when the file is scaffolded,
60	  and preserved by every converge after: `packs/claudinite-tasks/hash-minute.mjs`, a pure function of the repo full name that
61	  bootstrap stamps in and baselining re-derives), a `concurrency` group, a
62	  `workflow_dispatch` trigger (whose one `wake` input is how a task is forced,
63	  here or from another repo), and a call into the vendored scheduler run — no logic of its own
64	  (schema and behaviour changes ride the vendor refresh, not workflow edits). It
65	  is the repo's **only** cron; the executor's workflow beside it carries none. Work
66	  that had its own cron'd workflow becomes a **task**, and that workflow is deleted
67	  — its steps move into the task's worker. So does work with no cron at all: an
68	  event-driven or condition-gated job becomes a task declaring `trigger: 'request'`,
69	  woken by whatever knows the event happened.

1	Below are rules on how to work on this repo.
2	
3	## Standing owner decisions — settled, do not re-litigate
4	
5	- **Designing or describing what Claudinite is** — its unit of adoption is the *repository*, which
6	  declares packs, runs its own tasks and validates its own state; a per-user, per-machine framing
7	  (a Claude Code plugin, a developer's install) is a category error that invents costs the real
8	  shape does not have. (designing-describing-claudinite)
9	
10	- **Converging a work item to a terminal** — `task:status:done` and `task:status:rejected` both
11	  CLOSE the issue they stand on, marked or filed; a terminal is not a question, so an open issue
12	  wearing one is a torn write rather than a resting state, and the re-ask is clearing the
13	  status. (converging-work-item)
14	
15	- **A `docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md` whose system is now built** — delete it whole rather than trim
16	  it. Verify each section already lives in a module header or pack `README.md` first, and move an
17	  owner-decision record with its rationale onto the element's provenance file. Leave a doc
18	  describing work in flight alone. (docs-initiative-design)
19	
20	- **Sweeping a deleted design doc's `§`-numbered pointers** — re-point each at a pack README, or

import re
p='packs/claudinite-tasks/docs/PRINCIPLES.md'
s=open(p).read()
# Every citation quotes a test's title VERBATIM, so its punctuation is the test
# file's, not this document's.
titles=set()
import glob
for f in glob.glob('packs/claudinite-tasks/test/**/*.test.mjs', recursive=True):
    for m in re.finditer(r"test\((['\"])((?:\\.|(?!\1).)*)\1", open(f).read()):
        titles.add(m.group(2).replace("\\'", "'").replace('\\"', '"'))
fixed=0
def repair(m):
    global fixed
    body=m.group(1)
    if '.test.mjs: ' not in body: return m.group(0)

    if title in titles: return m.group(0)
    cand = title.replace(' - ', ' — ')
    if cand in titles:
        fixed += 1
        return f'`{file_}: {cand}`'
    return m.group(0)

open(p,'w').write(s)

entries.description:
Get logs for GitHub Actions workflow jobs.
Use this tool to retrieve logs for a specific job or all failed jobs in a workflow run.
For single job logs, provide job_id. For all failed jobs in a run, provide run_id with failed_only=true.

failed_only.description: When true, gets logs for all failed jobs in the workflow run specified by run_id. Requires run_id to be provided.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow job. Required when getting logs for a single job.

return_content.description: Returns actual log content instead of URLs

run_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run. Required when failed_only is true to get logs for all failed jobs in the run.

tail_lines.description: Number of lines to return from the end of the log

lastPrompt: lgtm

* Let every entry point survive its own exit

An entry point's catch that calls process.exit(1) after printing discards
whatever stdout has not drained. Piped to a slow reader, a run that logged
200,000 lines delivered 309 of them; setting process.exitCode = 1 and
letting the process end naturally delivered all 200,000, with the same
status. Each of these 27 guards already runs as its module's entry point
and waits on nothing after the catch, so there is nothing left to hurry.

Replaces #2082, whose diff predated the claudinite-tasks src/ move and so
conflicted against paths that no longer exist. The sweep is re-derived
against today's tree, which also covers entry points added since.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NDqxhAtTZPcyZWMp25QMnk

* Guard print-then-exit rather than sweep it again

The node pack has carried the rule since 2026-09-15 and the tree still held 34
print-then-exit sites, one of them a task worker added after #2082 swept the
class. A rule re-swept by hand is a check nobody wrote, so this adds the check
and finishes the sweep.

The check is a scope: "work" declaration in this repo's own local pack, over the
lines a change ADDS: the canon's node pack owns the prose but never activates
here (no package.json), so a check placed there would never run where the drift
keeps happening. Reading the change rather than the tree means no allowlist is
owed to the sanctioned holdouts - hook-runner.mjs exits from the write's own
callback, the two check runners decide their own status.

The sweep takes every remaining site where the print and the exit are adjacent
statements and the exit is not also the abort: process.exitCode with a return in
its place, and read-release-config's fail() becomes a throw its entry point
catches. The eight left are hook entry points and top-level try/catch blocks
whose control flow has to be reshaped rather than a token replaced; #2243 holds
them, and says why they are not in a sweep.

Refs #2243

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XteyrTKGWYdLwmHq6TdhRM

* Keep the new check's declaration beside the one main added

Refs #2225

Rebased onto main. Both sides appended to the same array in the local
pack's declared-checks.json - main's `pack-prose-paths-resolve` and this
branch's `print-then-exit` - and to four provenance logs, which are
append-only: every entry stands.

The four workers this change touches carry no provenance entry. Their
files are empty, so the tool requires the first entry to be `born`, and
writing one for a task this change did not create would be invented
history. The backfill owns them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NDqxhAtTZPcyZWMp25QMnk

* Let the runner wrap a task's worker, not every worker itself

A task declares `code_worker_mjs` instead of `code_work`: the module beside
task.json exporting `worker`, which the runner's own entry point imports and
calls. Never both - the two answer the same question about the same phase.

What every raw worker re-implemented now lives in worker-entry.mjs once: the
CLAUDINITE_* environment read into a parameters bag, `process.exitCode` rather
than a hard exit, the `<pack>/<task> failed:` line with the stack and the
`.triage` an error carries, the run's timing, and the queue's triage, requeue and
agent-request protocol rendered from a returned verdict. A module holds the work
and states what it found; the wrapping is the runner's.

The author-time check learns the field beside the runtime contract, because the
two read the same declaration from different sides and a check taught one of two
identical surfaces reads as strictness on the other.

No task is converted here. A member holding an older claudinite-tasks reads the
new key as absent, and its declaration then fails the contract for want of a work
step - so the shelf moves one convergence window after this lands, which #2258
holds behind it.

Refs #2258

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XteyrTKGWYdLwmHq6TdhRM

* Name the wrapped-form fixture after no real task

The rename main landed while this branch was open reached the fixtures in this
file; the case added here spelled `growth-extract`, which claudinite-growth owns.

Refs #2258

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XteyrTKGWYdLwmHq6TdhRM

* Convert every task to the wrapped worker form

All 20 tasks that declared `code_work: "node worker.mjs"` now declare
`code_worker_mjs` and export `worker(params)`. Nothing they do changes:
the same work runs, exits the same way and prints the same markers. What
goes is the copy of the wrapping each one carried - the environment
parsed by hand, the exit code, the failure line, the elapsed time, the
agent-request file - which now lives once in the runner's entry point.

The deferral in #2258 was wrong and is dropped: `computeVendorSet` walks
every declared pack from one canon snapshot and the writer lays it down
transactionally, so no member ever holds a converted declaration beside
an older reader of it. The lane split that argument rested on is
pack-versus-engine, and none of this is engine-side.

Three things the conversion needed:

- The bag gains `token` (the Action's own), `stepSummary`, and a
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` fallback for `repo` - each one a read every raw
  worker was already making for itself.
- A returned `{ triage }` now fails the run. The executor reads a park's
  routing only off a non-zero exit, so a worker that parked itself on a
  clean one was downgrading its own failure into a lane nobody watches.
- The two workflows that drive a worker directly - the canary rehearsal
  and the canon's pack-versions push - spawn the runner's entry point
  around it, which is what a real run does.

`consumer-safe-change` blocks on the `main` export the 17 wrapped
workers drop. Answered in the PR rather than with a shim, per the
owner's call: a task worker is spawned by path and never imported, so no
member can hold a consumer of that name.

Refs #2225

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XteyrTKGWYdLwmHq6TdhRM

* Record the reviewed exception for the dropped worker entry points

`consumer-safe-change` blocks on the `main` export the 17 wrapped workers
drop, and none of its three discharges fits: a task's worker is spawned by
path and never imported, and the old `main` took no arguments and read the
whole code-work environment, so no member can hold a consumer of that name.
A shim would trade a loud load-time error for a quiet runtime one, a
rehearsal fixture cannot speak about a name that is gone, and a migration
record would spend an agent session in every member converging to a no-op.

So it goes where this repo records a looked-at-and-fine: one `accept` entry
carrying the whole argument, beside the three already there. The check stays
blocking for everyone else.

lines: -// The member declaration's rename and reshape (#1252): `.claudinite-checks.json`
-// becomes `.claudinite-settings.json`, each pack's installed version moves onto that
-// pack's own entry, and the two blocks that had stopped saying anything come out.
-// WHY A RECORD AND NOT A CONVERGE. The file is the MEMBER'S — its packs, its rules,
-// its acceptances, its scheduler anchor. A converge writes files the canon owns; this
-// one it may only edit in place, once, which is exactly what a record is for.
-// WHY IT NEEDS NO CAPABILITY PROBE. The usual hazard — a record that needs engine
-// behaviour newer than the member's vendored worker — does not apply: the update
-// worker loads the engine-update flow out of the FRESH canon clone, and the
-// reshape op runs from that same clone. The member's own copy of the worker is only
-// asked to read its declaration before the converge, which it does under the old name
-// because that is still the name at that moment.
-// WHAT MAKES THE WINDOW SAFE. Every reader in the corpus tries both names, in
-// SETTINGS_FILES order (engine/settings-file.mjs), so a member is read correctly
-// whether or not this has run — which is what lets the rename land in one pass
-// instead of a phased stack. That tolerance is the thing this record exists to make
-// removable: it goes on #1640's window, a week after the advisory that reports the old name.
-export default {
-  id: 'settings-file-rename',

-  summary: '.claudinite-checks.json -> .claudinite-settings.json; pack versions onto their own entries; the retired "claudinite" and "maintenance" blocks folded into engineVersion and dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview; taskScheduler.endpoints renamed',
-  // Structural, and every rule of the reshape lives in the op rather than here —
-  // see applySettingsReshape in engine/migrations/registry.mjs.
-  reshapeSettings: true,
// torn rather than in flight. A converge writes the label and the close within
// seconds of each other, so an hour is far past any live transition.
export const TERMINAL_OPEN_MS = 3600e3;
-export const STUCK_BLOCKED_MS = 2 * 86400e3;
const ms = (t) => (t == null ? null : new Date(t).getTime());
const idle = (item, now) => ms(now) - (ms(item.updated_at) ?? ms(item.created_at) ?? ms(now));
+ `${wedged ? 'without the work moving — the session kept beating, but every beat said the same thing' : 'with no activity'} — `
+ `the agent session that claimed it${sessionNote ? ` (${sessionNote})` : ''} never converged it. Parking it for a human.`;
-// Rule C — THE STUCK-DEPENDENCY SWEEP (F14). The stale-ready rule cannot see this
-// at all: a blocked item is never ready. So a blocked item whose blockers have not
-// resolved past the bound gets an escalation COMMENT and nothing else — labels
-// untouched, so the item still proceeds by itself the moment its blockers resolve,
-// and a human who decides it is dead closes it by hand.
-// THE BOUND IS IDLENESS, NEVER AGE (owner, 2026-09-22). Measured from `created_at`
-// the rule had no terminating condition: once an item crossed two days it matched
-// on every pass for the rest of its life, and the sweep carried no once-only guard,
-// so a chain link waiting on a long review collected one comment per run forever.
-// Measured from the item's own last activity, the comment this rule posts resets
-// the clock it is read from, which makes the comment its own guard: the next one is
-// two idle days away, and a person or a run touching the item pushes it further out.
-// Sleeping items (a future `Not-before`, blockers closed) never match: waiting for
-// a time is the mechanism working.
-export function stuckBlockedItems(open = [], now, { stateOf = () => null, boundMs = STUCK_BLOCKED_MS } = {}) {
-  return open.filter((i) => {
-    if (!isStatus(i, STATUS_BLOCKED)) return false;
-    const { blockedBy } = parseWorkItemBody(i.body);
-    if (!blockedBy.length) return false;
-    if (blockedBy.every((n) => stateOf(n) === 'closed')) return false;
-    return idle(i, now) >= boundMs;

-  `This work item has been blocked on ${unresolved.map((n) => `#${n}`).join(', ')} for over `
-  + `${Math.round(STUCK_BLOCKED_MS / 86400e3)} days. Nothing here is stuck mechanically — it will proceed by itself the moment those close — `

// Rule D — THE STATELESS-ITEM REPAIR. An open work item whose labels decode to no
// status at all is off the state machine entirely: a torn label swap's
// leavings (an executor that died between the remove and the add), invisible to
-// THE REPAIR PHASE of the scheduler run (docs/PRINCIPLES.md) - the recovery that
+// THE REPAIR PHASE of the scheduler run (docs/PRINCIPLES.md) — the recovery that
// used to run once a day as a task of its own, planned here as ops the same run
// applies before it asks any task whether it wants to run.

+// wrong — a label swap that tore, a session that died, a park nobody answered, a

-// whole reason this is a phase of the run and not a task behind it - a task's own
+// whole reason this is a phase of the run and not a task behind it — a task's own

lines: -# task-janitor
-## What this task is
-A **fallback**. Every rule it runs repairs something that already went wrong — a
-label swap that tore, a session that died, a park nobody answered, a pull request
-somebody resolved without closing the item behind it. No stage of the healthy flow
-of a task runs here: an item the machinery handled correctly is settled by whoever
-handled it, long before this task's next pass. A new rule is therefore a claim that
-a failure mode exists and that nothing nearer to it can close the item out.
-It reads only OPEN items. An item somebody closed is finished, park label and all:
-a person ending a park by closing its issue has answered it, and this task neither
-reopens nor re-labels nor re-announces one.
-## Why the declaration reads as it does
-Carried over from the declaration's comments when it became `task.json`.
-basics task: task-janitor — the THIRD responsibility of the scheduled-task
-machinery (owner, 2026-08-06). The scheduler run CREATES and readies work items, the
-executor EXECUTES exactly the one item it picked, and this task — alone —
-cleans up after both: items stuck ready past their period, items left wearing
-no state label by a torn transition, and a health review of the open set.
-Neither the scheduler run nor the executor does any of that; a task execution cares only
-about its own item, and recovery lives here, in code, once a day.
-It also sweeps what the retired slot mechanism left behind: the last slot runs
-filed `[claudinite-task]` dispatch issues in members, and nothing else closes
-them out. That half retires when the fleet's are gone, not before.
-The scheduler run reclaims a dead executor claim itself, hourly — this task is the
-slower backstop for what the scheduler run's deterministic label mechanics cannot see.
-`agent_model: 'none'` + code_work: the whole pass is deterministic code the
-executor runs as code-work — no agent phase, fully automatic.
-The queue's own health is what this reads, and the queue is exactly what keeps
-moving on a repo that is otherwise silent — so no repo-side condition gates it.
-One repo-wide issue search plus a handful of label/comment writes — seconds.
-## When it runs
-Daily at most, and then only when the open queue holds something one of its rules
-would claim: `queue-needs-sweep` in `preconditions.mjs` asks the sweep's own
-question off the open work-item list, so a healthy queue files no item at all. A
-park of any kind holds it, as does an item off the state machine, a terminal status
-standing open, a dead agent claim, a ready item nobody picked, or a blocked one past
-its bound. A queue that could not be read is an error and parks the run - never a
-decline.
-  "$schema": "../../task.schema.json",
-  "id": "task-janitor",

-  "description": "Cleans up after the scheduler and the executor: re-queues items stuck past their period, repairs items a torn transition left without a state label, and reviews the health of the open set.",
-  "trigger": "schedule",
-  "preconditions": [
-    "schedule:at-most-daily",
-    "queue-needs-sweep"
-  "expected_outcome": "no_code_changes",
-  "code_worker_mjs": "worker.mjs",
-  "code_work_timeout": 300
-// The task-janitor's code-work — the whole task (agent_model: none). The ONE
-// home of dispatch-issue recovery and health review, moved out of the
-// scheduler's hourly run (owner, 2026-08-06: scheduler creates, executor
-// executes its one issue, janitor cleans up). This file is the I/O shell; the
-// verdicts are the pure rules in the vendored engine (dispatch.mjs), so what
-// counts as stale, dead or lost is decided in exactly one place.
-// Three backstops, in this order:
-//   1. STALE — a dispatch open past ~2 of its own scheduling periods →
-//      escalation comment, drop the ready label, add `needs-human`. Once — an
-//      already-escalated issue is never re-announced.
-//   2. DEAD CLAIM — `agent-running` with no activity for ~3h → the session that
-//      claimed it died; comment, drop `agent-running`, add `needs-human`.
-//   3. RE-ARM — armed but untouched past the grace window → the trigger event
-//      was lost, so remove and re-add its ready label to emit a fresh one.
-// Stale wins over re-arm, so an issue converging to triage is never put back
-// into circulation.
-// The daily cadence is a stated trade (it was hourly when it lived in the
-// scheduler): a lost trigger event or a dead claim now waits up to a day for
-// recovery. That is the price of the responsibility split, and the owner chose
-// it — recurring recovery is cleanup, and cleanup is nobody's job but this one.
-// It ends with a HEALTH REVIEW: one line per open dispatch state, so the run
-// log answers "how is the task machinery doing" at a glance.

-  SCHEDULER_LABELS,

-import { ensureLabels } from '../../src/world/github.mjs';
-import { searchIssues, comment, addLabel, removeLabel, listComments } from '../../src/world/github.mjs';

-// helpers below log too; `worker` takes the one the runner built.
-let log = console.log;

-// the rules read. Repo-wide and open-only — the scheduler's own per-family

-    created_at: i.created_at, updated_at: i.updated_at, comments: i.comments ?? 0,

-export async function sweep(gh, repo, now) {

-  // over the post-sweep label states as this run leaves them.
-  const names = (i) => (i.labels ?? []).map((l) => (typeof l === 'string' ? l : l?.name)).filter(Boolean);

-    + `this run escalated ${result.stale.length}, reclaimed ${result.deadClaims.length}, re-armed ${result.rearmed.length}`);
-  return result;
-// WHICH SWEEP is the repo's dispatch mode (docs/PRINCIPLES.md): the two

-// find nothing in one of them and a janitor that ran the wrong one would find
-// nothing at all — and report a clean bill of health either way. One repo, one
-// mechanism, one sweep.
-export async function worker({ root, repo, gh, log: runLog }) {
-  log = runLog;
-  const { loadConfig } = await import('../../../../engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs');
-  const config = loadConfig(root);

attachment.content:
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- backfilling-provenance: Filling a pack's empty provenance files from its history. Use when a pack under packs/ or .claudinite/local/packs/ carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill or write a pack's provenance.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- changing-pack-elements: What a change to a pack's element owes - the entry on its provenance file, which kind, and how to append it - and what a pack's README carries. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md, skills, checks, tasks, manifest, README or provenance folder, in a repo's local pack or on a canon's shelf.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- extract-from-instructions: Convert instruction prose somebody already wrote into pack carriers, leaving the prose file a thin routing map. Use when adopting Claudinite on a repo that already carries a CLAUDE.md, when a person wants their machine-local instructions carried properly, or when asked to convert instruction prose into a pack.
- extract-packs-from-a-project: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or a file from the web in a session — exact bytes over a summarizing fetch, and what a 403 or an egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl, and when a fetch is denied.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve a repo's own comments as a pass of their own: delete, correct, add the why. Use when working a repo's comments deliberately (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own. Use when asked to make a repo do something with a technology nobody there has used yet (host it on X, send through Y, publish to Z), or to "research how to do this correctly" and "create a skill" for it.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner approves the current branch or PR, or asks to merge or land it into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production. Use when designing a larger element, when filing a migration plan's chain, when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- revalidating-rules: Re-probe the pack rules whose truth lives outside the repository — harness tool contracts, token reach, whether an MCP tool exists, a platform's behaviour — and correct the ones that have gone stale. Use when a revalidation sweep runs over a corpus of packs, or when asked whether a rule's environmental claim still holds.
- running-the-suite: Running this repo's test suite — the one command that covers it, reading a run's output from a file instead of re-running it, iterating on the tests an edit touches, and staging a new test file before certifying a run. Use before any node --test.
- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- working-with-generated-files: Working with a file a test or tool generates — naming it, changing the generator rather than the file, and resolving its merge conflicts by regenerating. Loaded for any edit of a GENERATED file.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: How a plan's phases are ordered so nothing stalls mid-run. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan (including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file), when asked to run a plan as a chain of ad-hoc tasks, and when working through a plan's tracking issue.

lines: -import { test } from 'node:test';
-import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
-import { terms } from '../../tasks/task-janitor/preconditions.mjs';
-import { AGENT_LEASH_MS, STUCK_BLOCKED_MS, TERMINAL_OPEN_MS } from '../../src/recover/janitor-rules.mjs';
-// task-janitor's own gate. The janitor is the fallback lane, so the term's whole
-// risk is a WRONG DECLINE — a repair nobody is asked to make — and every case here
-// is about what it must NOT sleep through.
-const NOW_MS = Date.parse('2026-09-20T12:00:00Z');
-const NOW = new Date(NOW_MS).toISOString();
-const ago = (ms) => new Date(NOW_MS - ms).toISOString();
-const HOUR = 3600e3;
-const item = (over = {}) => ({
-  number: 7, title: '[claudinite-work] p/t', body: 'packs/p/tasks/t/task.md\n', state: 'open',
-  labels: ['task:status:waiting-for-executor', 'task:origin:planned'],
-  created_at: ago(HOUR), closed_at: null, updated_at: ago(HOUR), ...over,
-const ask = (open) => terms['queue-needs-sweep'].holds({ queue: { open } }, { now: NOW });
-test('a queue where every item is live, statused and inside its clocks declines', () => {
-  const verdict = ask([
-    item(),
-    item({ number: 8, labels: ['task:status:running-agent'], updated_at: ago(HOUR) }),
-    item({ number: 9, labels: ['task:status:running-executor'] }),
-  assert.equal(verdict.holds, false);
-  assert.match(verdict.reason, /3 open/, 'the reason says what it looked at, so a wrong decline is readable in the log');
-test('an empty queue declines — no rule of the janitor has a domain', () => {
-  assert.equal(ask([]).holds, false);
-test('a parked item always holds: four rules read a park, and each needs a read this term does not make', () => {
-  for (const park of ['failure', 'action', 'decision', 'approval']) {
-    const verdict = ask([item({ labels: [`task:status:needs-human-${park}`] })]);
-    assert.equal(verdict.holds, true, `a ${park} park must wake the janitor`);
-test('an item off the state machine holds — the torn label swap is rule D', () => {
-  assert.equal(ask([item({ labels: ['task:origin:planned'] })]).holds, true);
-test('a terminal status standing open past its bound holds', () => {
-  const inFlight = ask([item({ labels: ['task:status:done'], updated_at: ago(TERMINAL_OPEN_MS / 2) })]);
-  assert.equal(inFlight.holds, false, 'a converge writes the label and the close seconds apart — that is not torn yet');
-  const torn = ask([item({ labels: ['task:status:done'], updated_at: ago(TERMINAL_OPEN_MS * 2) })]);
-  assert.equal(torn.holds, true);
-test('a dead agent claim holds exactly at the leash, not only past it', () => {
-  const running = (age) => item({ labels: ['task:status:running-agent'], updated_at: ago(age) });
-  assert.equal(ask([running(AGENT_LEASH_MS - 1)]).holds, false);
-  assert.equal(ask([running(AGENT_LEASH_MS)]).holds, true, 'the rule claims at >=, and the tick lands ON the boundary as often as either side');
-test('a blocked item past the stuck bound holds; one whose wait is a time does not', () => {
-  const blocked = (over) => item({ labels: ['task:status:blocked'], created_at: ago(STUCK_BLOCKED_MS + HOUR), ...over });
-  assert.equal(ask([blocked({ body: 'packs/p/tasks/t/task.md\nBlocked-by: #4\n' })]).holds, true);
-  assert.equal(ask([blocked({ body: 'packs/p/tasks/t/task.md\nNot-before: 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z\n' })]).holds, false,
-    'waiting for a time is the mechanism working, not a repair');
-test('a ready item nobody picked for two of its periods holds', () => {
-  const ready = (age) => item({ updated_at: ago(age), created_at: ago(age) });
-  assert.equal(ask([ready(HOUR * 36)]).holds, false);
-  assert.equal(ask([ready(HOUR * 24 * 3)]).holds, true);
-test('an unreadable queue is an error, never a decline', () => {
-  const verdict = terms['queue-needs-sweep'].holds({ queue: { error: 'the work-item list could not be read at page 2 (502)' } }, { now: NOW });

-  assert.match(verdict.error, /502/, 'the reason the read failed travels to the failure park');

I have to correct the record before anything else, because I told you the same wrong thing twice.

**That CI failure was mine, not pre-existing.** My check was broken: `git stash` doesn't stash untracked files, so the "clean main" run I compared against still had my new modules sitting in the tree. Against a real `origin/main` worktree the test passes. I should have used a worktree the first time; asserting "identical on main" from a stash was exactly the kind of inferred verdict this repo has a rule against.

The cause turned out to be more useful than the symptom: **the branch was ten commits behind main**, and three of those commits collided with this work.

- `engine/pack_loader/token-estimate.mjs` simply did not exist at my base. The lane-shim test was telling the truth about a module main already carried.
- **#2225 converted every task to a wrapped-worker contract** while this branch was open — including the janitor's, which had gained a `preconditions.mjs` and a test for it. Those are now deleted in the shape main left them, not the shape I found them in.
- **#2138 retired the frequency door** and **#1920 the queue's legacy tolerances**. The orphaned-park case I ported carried a `grow_with_claudinite` fixture whose rename mapping is gone; main had already moved its own copy to a spelling that still resolves, and mine now matches.

The provenance files are the other thing worth naming: main's backfill filled them with history derived from the pack's real commits while my base had them empty, so I had written `born` entries from thin evidence. Main's win; mine are gone, with only this change's own entries appended after.

Rebased, force-pushed, and:

- **Suite: 3920 pass, 0 fail.** No caveat this time, and `engine-pack-lane-shims` passes.
- **`check_the_world`: no blocking findings.** The two it did raise were mine — a fixture spelling a real pack name needs its `@real-entity` marker on the line itself, not above it — and are fixed. Every remaining advisory predates the branch.
- Three citations in `writing-tasks` pointed at module paths the earlier `src/` move had stranded; fixed while the file was open.

CI is running on the rebased head. I'll merge when it's green, then do the local task run and the canary force you asked for — the canary matters more now, since main's worker-contract change and this one land on members together.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

The user (owner of the `missingbulb/Claudinite` repo, [REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL]) began with a design question — "What if we collapse the janitor task into the dispatcher functionality, to improve its ability to pick up tasks?" — which evolved through discussion into an approved, implemented change. Explicit requests in order:
   - Discuss/analyze collapsing the `task-janitor` task into the scheduler run; answer whether the simulator tests use the janitor as a moving part.
   - Enumerate all state-transition rules a merged dispatcher-janitor would run; then rewrite that list with full label names, pseudocode conditions, simplified writes, legacy label management split out, and newlines between clauses.
   - Verify four claims: one-issues-read sufficiency; state-changes-then-scheduling = one pass; minimize log comments (keep only terminals and human-needed explanations); whether a missed heartbeat affects a running Actions job.
   - "I think I gave you enough to plan the merge and eliminate the janitor. Please go ahead."
   - "I think doing all A-D steps in one PR is ok. And doing E,F in this session after we merge is ok. Only thing we postpone is G... verify the plan with a small fable subagent and tell me the outcome."
   - Decisions: **no changes to heartbeat or executor Actions**; instead defer a task-TTL suggestion (later withdrawn); **delete rule C** (later reversed to "Rule C should be fixed"); **keep the legacy slot sweep as a placeholder but eliminate long-retired items from the action**.
   - "Make sure to consider execution times for the dispatcher after the merge. We still need to make sure it runs as efficiently as possible."
   - "Don't file the follow up TTL work."
   - "lgtm" (merge the change into main via the `merge-to-main` skill).
   - "After you merge - can you test tasks run locally (and don't break) and also force update to claudinitecanaty and test tasks run there?"

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Claudinite: a repository-scoped agent-instruction framework with packs, vendored engine, declared checks, provenance logs, skills forced by path/tool guards.
   - Work-item queue as GitHub issues; labels are state (`task:status:*`, `task:origin:*`).
   - Three-responsibility split (owner decision 2026-08-06): scheduler run creates/readies, executor executes one item, janitor cleans up.
   - `planSchedulerRun` (pure planner) + `schedulerRun` (I/O shell); ops applied by the shell.
   - Repair phase: recovery folded into the scheduler run, running **before** the ask, with effects threaded into the in-memory item list.
   - Confirm-gated ops (fresh re-read before writing) for transient-premise rules (stateless, abandoned, unclosed) — #1104.
   - Legacy label tolerances (`task:ready`, `task:blocked`, `needs-human`, `outcome:*`), `spellingsOf`, `clearStatus`/`swapStatus`.
   - Executing leash (60m), agent leash (3h), heartbeat (15m), executor job `timeout-minutes: 350`.
   - GitHub `since` parameter filters on **updated** time; `state=open`/`state=closed` listings.
   - The simulator (`test/sim/`) as the mechanism's executable spec; scenarios S1–S81; `coverage.test.mjs` two-way citation drift guard against `docs/PRINCIPLES.md`.
   - CI recursion guard: `on: pull_request` does not fire for a PR authored by the app's own token; remedy is `workflow_dispatch`.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`packs/claudinite-tasks/src/schedule/repair.mjs`** (NEW) — the repair phase planner. Exports `planRepair({items, tasks, now, progressAt, resolutionOf, doneAfter, isRequest, stateOf})` returning `{ops, closed}`. Emits op kinds:
     ```
     //   { kind: 'escalate', issue, from, to, body }        status -> a park, item stays open
     //   { kind: 'retire',   issue, from, to, body, close } status -> a terminal, issue closes
     //   { kind: 'close-terminal', issue, body, close }     the close a torn transition never made
     //   { kind: 'note', issue, body }                      a comment and nothing else
     ```
     Each op carries `rule:` ('superseded', 'orphaned', 'ended', 'abandoned', 'unclosed', 'stale-ready', 'dead-agent', 'stateless', 'stuck-dependency'). Threading:
     ```js
     const threadable = (op) => !op.confirm;
     function threadEffect(item, op) {
       if (op.from) { const gone = new Set(spellingsOf(op.from)); item.labels = item.labels.filter((l) => !gone.has(l)); }
       if (op.to && !item.labels.includes(op.to)) item.labels.push(op.to);
       if (op.kind === 'retire') { item.state = 'closed'; item.closed_at = op.at; }
     }
     ```
     Torn-adoption guard: `for (const item of statelessItems(open)) { if (isRequest(item.number)) continue; ... }`. Contains a documented "legacy cleanup" section as the placeholder home (no live rules).

   - **`packs/claudinite-tasks/src/schedule/repair-rules.mjs`** (renamed from `src/recover/janitor-rules.mjs`, then moved from `src/recover/` to `src/schedule/` to satisfy the `tasks-stage-barriers` check) — the pure rules A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I plus `doneRunLookup`. Rule C restored with idleness bound:
     ```js
     export function stuckBlockedItems(open = [], now, { stateOf = () => null, boundMs = STUCK_BLOCKED_MS } = {}) {
       return open.filter((i) => {
         if (!isStatus(i, STATUS_BLOCKED)) return false;
         const { blockedBy } = parseWorkItemBody(i.body);
         if (!blockedBy.length) return false;
         if (blockedBy.every((n) => stateOf(n) === 'closed')) return false;
         return idle(i, now) >= boundMs;   // was: ms(now) - ms(i.created_at)
       });
     }
     ```

   - **`packs/claudinite-tasks/src/schedule/run.mjs`** — wired the phase in before the orphan reap; added `progressAt`/`resolutionOf`/`doneAfter`/`stateOf` seams; added `REPAIR_KINDS = ['escalate','retire','close-terminal','note']` and `applyRepairOp(...)` with `stillHolds()` confirm logic; added `phase('repair')` timer; two listings:
     ```js
     const items = [
       ...await listWorkItems(gh, repo, { state: 'open' }),
       ...await listWorkItems(gh, repo, { state: 'closed', since }),
     ];
     ```
     `listWorkItems` gained `state` param. Label-ensure narrowed: `if (repairOps.some((o) => o.to)) await ensureLabels(...)`.

   - **`packs/claudinite-tasks/src/items/run-record.mjs`** — `scheduler: Object.freeze(['list', 'repair', 'ask', 'drain'])`.

# claudinite-tasks — scheduled work

Everything whose subject is task work: the work-item queue, the executor, the task contract and
its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, and the delivery lane a task's output
lands through. Declaring this pack is what gives a repo scheduled work; a repo that does not
declare it runs none, which is a supported state rather than a degraded one.

The mechanism itself, from the state machine and the generator to the executor's protocol,
urgency, forcing and recovery, is [`docs/PRINCIPLES.md`](docs/PRINCIPLES.md); authoring a task is
the `writing-tasks` skill's subject. This file is the pack's own map.

## Layout

Every module sits in the ROLE it plays, and the graph between the roles is
one-directional. `contract/` and `items/` are what everything agrees on and name no
stage; `world/` holds the only modules that reach outside the run; the stages sit on
top of those and never import each other sideways or upwards. The `tasks-stage-barriers`
and `tasks-world-edges-live-in-world` checks are what hold the shape.

| Path | The role |
|---|---|
| `src/contract/` | what a task DECLARES and what its declaration means: the declaration's shape and defaults, the term vocabulary and the precondition seam every caller asks through, cadence and anchor arithmetic, the auto-merge policy engine, task discovery, dormancy |
| `src/items/` | the work item as DATA, over the vocabulary and grammar `public/` defines: the queue listings, the run record, the pick order over the open queue, the heartbeat |
| `src/world/` | the only outward edges, each a named port — `github.mjs` (every REST path this pack calls, as a named operation), `actions.mjs` (the runner's environment) with `hold.mjs` and the three env bags beside it, `sessions.mjs` (the routine fire that starts an agent), `git.mjs`, `processes.mjs`, `clock.mjs` |
| `src/signals/` | the collectors a precondition is handed, read through the ports and described in the contract's terms |
| `src/schedule/` | the tick: the repair phase that runs first, then which declared tasks have a window open and the items filed for them |
| `src/execute/` | the executor: claiming a ready item, running its code-work, handing it to an agent session |
| `src/session/` | what runs INSIDE a work-item session: converging the item, verifying its outcome, the exec record, dispatch resolution, and the automerge verdict as a command |
| `src/deliver/` | turning a run's output into a landed pull request or a regenerated file |
| `src/recover/` | repair: the queue's repair rules, workflow-failure escalation, the dead-run continuation |
| `src/adopt/` | what an adopting repo receives: the workflows converged from the stubs, the per-repo cron minute |
| `queue/` | `tasks/implement-request/`, the engine's own built-in task; the spec is `public/implement-request.md` |
| `stubs/` | the two workflow files an adopting repo receives |
| `public/` | **everything outside this pack may reference** — the vocabulary and grammar `src/` builds on, the import surface, and the documents a routine reads. See below |
| `tasks/` | this pack's own tasks: `usage-fold` (it folds this mechanism's run records and outcome labels), `tasks-usage-fold` (what the machinery itself cost - runs, billed minutes, API calls, outcomes, parks, latencies) and `verify-production` (coded production validations - URL probes judged as code-work) |
| `worldRules/` | the task-declaration checks |
| `workRules/` | the armed-auto-merge gate (`automerge-policy-scope`) |
| `declared-checks.json` | `tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` — the guard over this pack's published surface, which runs wherever the pack is declared |
| `test/` | the unit suite, mirroring `src/`, and `test/sim/` — the simulator and its scenario suite, the mechanism's executable spec |
| `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` | the mechanism as claims, each citing the test that proves it |
| `src/deliver/deliver-pr.md` | the landing procedure every PR-delivering task's worker is pointed at, beside the lane it describes |

## `public/` — everything outside this pack may reference

One folder, one promise: **a name in `public/` does not move.** Everything a routine reads, another
pack imports or a member's own local pack names lives here, and nothing else of this pack is
addressable from outside. A member's `.github/workflows/` runs the entry points under `src/`
named by the two stubs, which are this pack's own files and not an outside caller.

Another pack's code may import `packs/claudinite-tasks/public/*` and nothing else of this pack;
the `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory, and no other pack gains an
equivalent surface by existing. **A member's own `.claudinite/local/packs/**` reads it the same
way**, through its mount (`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/public/*`): the nightly
converge replaces `.claudinite/shared/` and may never touch a member's own packs, so an import
aimed anywhere else is one this repository cannot repair when the layout behind it moves.

### Documents named from outside

| Path | What names it |
|---|---|
| `instructions.md` | a repo's work-item routine, as a stored prompt in its console settings |
| `implement-request.md` | the machine block of every issue adopted into the queue |

### Modules other packs import

Three of the five are the DEFINITION, and `src/` imports them from here: the vocabulary, the
grammar over it and the GitHub client import nothing of `src/`. The other two are the
machinery's own operations under a stable name.

| Module | What it publishes |
|---|---|
| `task-constants.mjs` | every value the queue writes and reads: the work item's labels, markers and body fields, the leases, the commit trailers, the declaration defaults, the pack's own parameters, the two workflow file names |
| `work-item-grammar.mjs` | the parse and serialize over that vocabulary — the title grammar that is an item's identity, the status and outcome decode over its labels (every legacy spelling included), the body fields, the machine block, the commit trailer |
| `github.mjs` | the GitHub client (`makeGh` and the run's call count), `dispatchWorkflow`, and the tracker issue a recurring task logs every run to |
| `delivery.mjs` | `deliverGenerated` — a regenerated file landed on a pull request that lands itself — and the landing lane's five names for a worker that lands its own pull request |
| `task-declaration.mjs` | the declaration's executable contract: the loader, its validation, the precondition evaluator the executor runs at pick, and the auto-merge policy engine |

A module publishes **named** exports rather than `export *`. A consumer needing something absent
asks for the named export to be added here, never a deeper import, which
`tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` refuses. Who reads each name
is derived on demand: `node packs/claudinite-canon-curation/pack-surface.mjs packs/claudinite-tasks`
renders the surface and its consumers from the tree.

A pack whose **non-task** code reads any of the modules above declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`. A
pack's `tasks/` folder needs no declaration: a mount without this pack carries no `tasks/` at all,
since a task folder is inert without the queue that runs it.

## Adoption

The two workflow files and the routine endpoints cannot converge into place — `.github/workflows/`
is the one directory a member's nightly update may never write — so they are scaffolded once, at
adoption, by the `adopt-pack` skill. They are static from then on: the per-repo cron minute and
anchor hours are written once, secrets travel as one fixed line, and the `run:` lines name mount
pack paths behind which everything converges nightly.

## Checks

| Rule | Confidence | Dimension | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task-declaration-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `task-code-work-env` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `automerge-policy-scope` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `executor-workflow-secrets` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
| `tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` | high | correctness | declared check: blocking |
| `repo-variables-through-the-bag` | high | correctness | declared check: blocking |

`tasks-pack-read-through-its-surface` is this pack's, not the canon's, because the consumers that
can get it wrong are members: it scans a repo's own `packs/` **and** its `.claudinite/local/packs/`,
the tree no converge may rewrite, so a deep import written there is caught in that repo's own run
rather than when it crashes.

`repo-variables-through-the-bag` — a module reads a repository variable over the REST variables
API, which the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` is refused on in every member (403, and no `permissions:` key
grants it), so the read never answers. Every repository variable already travels in the executor's
vars bag: a task's code-work finds it in `process.env`, engine code reads `varsBag(env)`.

The first two are relevance-first — inert until the repo carries a `tasks/<name>/task.json` of its own; the third is self-gating on the branch's own arming trailer.

- `task-declaration-shape` — a task declaration the scheduler reads is incomplete or illegal — no `trigger` saying who mints an occurrence, an unknown condition, an illegal value — so the task never fires or fires wrong.
- `task-code-work-env` — a task reads a `CLAUDINITE_*` variable code-work never sets, so a parameter (a scope filter, a dry-run switch) silently never arrives and the run goes green in its most dangerous mode.
- `executor-workflow-secrets` — the executor workflow does not pass a secret the tasks of this repo's packs declare, so the queue picks the item up and only the run finds out the secret is not there. The list is the tasks' alone; an invocation endpoint's `tokenSecret` is config, stamped by the converge and reported by the invocation call itself. Advisory because the remedy is a human-merged PR to `.github/workflows/`, the one fix a member's own machinery cannot make.
- `automerge-policy-scope` — a branch that stamped the `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy` trailer (its run intends to land its own PR) carries a diff its declared policy does not cover, which is exactly the unreviewed change the policy exists to stop.
